name: Instrument state diagram
reader_question: Which legal or administrative states can this instrument occupy, which one is current, and which transitions are permitted?
relationship: Discrete states of one instrument linked by labelled, directed transitions; one state is current.
use_when: The reader needs to know what can happen next to an instrument, not when it happened
Transitions have a named trigger such as a vote, a date or an order
avoid_when: The order and dates of events are the point — use a timeline
Quantities move between the states — use conversion-flow

data_contract.notes: Date at which the current state is read
3–6 states in layout order; row 2 runs right to left
Directed, labelled by trigger; endpoints must be declared states; no duplicates

units: No quantities; the only date is the as-of date of the current state.

editable: State boxes, arrows and trigger labels as native shapes and text
Fill and outline of each state
not_data_bound: States and transitions are drawn shapes; editing the fixture and re-running the build is the way to change structure
Arrow geometry is computed and not connected to the boxes as PowerPoint connectors

table_alternative: A transition table (from state, to state, trigger).
variations: Terminal states marked in the note line
limitations: Up to six states in two rows; larger lifecycles need a table or a split into two exhibits
Only transitions between adjacent rows or neighbours are routed; the layout order is chosen by the author
The diagram shows permitted transitions, not how often or when they occur

excluded_alternatives.reason: Adds branching logic the state record does not contain; use condition-tree for decisions
Answers when, not which transitions are possible
